findings.where: First screen, desktop: the 'Write to me' note in the left margin, the page's one call to action
findings.fault: The only way to get in touch is a small red scrawl outside the content column. It sits beside the hero's last line, far from the heading and photo the eye reads first, and looks like a doodle rather than something to click. On a squint it has the lightest weight of anything on the first screen, below the aqueduct sketch and the photo. It gives no email address and no label saying it writes an email, and since no footer is drawn, the page never shows the address anywhere.
findings.who_objects: The bank official who has decided Mark may fit and wants to write. They look for a contact route at the end of the pitch and in the body column, not in the binding margin. A procurement reader also expects to see and copy a plain email address.

findings.where: Nav bar (the binding): the aqueduct mark and the 'MMM INFRA' wordmark, at both widths; and the palette tile, which holds neither logo colour
findings.fault: The logo is recoloured gold on the oxblood binding. Its grey #404040 arches and blue #0070C0 Georgia wordmark are gone, and Mark holds no such gold version. The palette tile also leaves out both logo colours: they are neither given a job nor declared logo-only. The site's one fixed brand asset is the thing this direction changes.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose logo the brief says stays. A returning contact who knows MMM Infra by its blue wordmark would not recognise the site at once. The layout round would inherit a logo version that was never approved.

findings.where: Page ground: the ruled lines and the double margin line, compared with the Texture and Palette tiles
findings.fault: The tiles promise pale blue feints (#93B3D3) and a red margin (#B8322B), the marks that make paper read as a legal pad. On the page the rules render a dull grey-olive and the double margin line a dark brown. The page reads as yellow paper with grey lines, not a legal pad, and the tile contradicts its own palette.
findings.who_objects: Mark, who chose the legal pad for its legal look. The layout round, which would take its values from a tile that doesn't match its own render.

findings.where: The 32 px ruled grid applied to all text: the article heading 'The World's Best Public- / Private Partnership Law' and the handwritten pull quote at desktop (and the pull quote's four lines at phone); the palette captions (name, hex, role); the texture, type-pair and motion notes
findings.fault: Every line is forced onto a 32 px rule whatever its size. Two-line headings and the quote get 64 px between lines and fall apart into separate lines. Small captions come out double-spaced, so each swatch's name, hex and role sit as far apart as the next swatch row and seem to belong to it. The same article heading is set tight at phone and loose at desktop.
findings.who_objects: An article reader, who loses the heading as one statement. Angélique, whose posts' headings and quotes would all break this way. The layout round, which gets no rule for display type on the grid.

findings.where: Article specimen: the pull quote 'Whichever PPP Law I am currently working on with a client country!' set in Nanum Pen Script
findings.fault: The tile's own rule says the hand is one note per view and never body text, but a whole pull quote is set in it. On an article page it would compete with the margin note. A stand-in handwriting font for Mark's words makes his considered point read as a casual scribble.
findings.who_objects: The official reading Mark's article for judgement: a key line in a novelty hand undercuts it. Mark, whose handwriting the font only stands in for.

findings.where: Article specimen: the lecture row 'Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the ‘Abundance’ Challenge · Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF', at both widths
findings.fault: The row's bottom rule runs along the baseline of its last line and cuts through the descenders, so it looks like an underline on that line only. The two-line link has no other link cue, so whether the title is clickable depends on that accidental line. At phone the date column squeezes to three lines.
findings.who_objects: A visitor looking for Mark's talks, the strongest proof of standing for a development-bank reader: the row looks broken and its link uncertain.

findings.where: Hero: the tilted photo print with its paperclip and drop shadow, at both widths
findings.fault: The portrait is a skewed snapshot clipped on with a cast shadow. That is a scrapbook trope close to the warm-craft look the direction card says to avoid. The shadow also gives a static photo a lifted, movable look (the parts map flags it as possibly actable).
findings.who_objects: The senior official, who expects the advisor's face presented plainly. A clipped holiday-style print reads as a hobby page, not a counsel's working paper.

findings.where: Hero copy: the italic line 'Over 40 years of international infrastructure experience.'
findings.fault: The second line of the pitch is given to a size claim with nothing checkable behind it, while the first screen names no region, no body Mark advised beyond one World Bank role, and no recent work. It is set apart as its own italic statement, which gives it the most weight of anything below the heading.
findings.who_objects: A procurement-minded MDB official, who judges experience by project kind, region and named bodies and discounts a years count. Feel the CV rules out size words.

findings.where: Style tile as a whole: the button deliverable; and the 'Replay the note' control in the motion sketch
findings.fault: The brief asks for a button, but the tile shows none. Its only actions are the margin scrawl and 'Replay the note', a button drawn as an underlined link, which borrows the link's look for an action. The layout round has no button treatment for places the margin note can't go, such as a form submit or a 'Download CV'.
findings.who_objects: The layout round's designer, who must invent the button this tile was meant to fix. Angélique, who will need a standard action when Mark adds a PDF.

findings.where: Phone, all sections: right margin against left margin
findings.fault: Content sits about 56 px from the left edge but only about 14 px from the right. The photo print, the palette swatches, the texture swatch and the motion box nearly touch the screen edge, so the column looks shoved right rather than set on a pad.
findings.who_objects: An official opening the link on a phone between meetings: the cramped right edge looks unfinished.

findings.where: Nav bar, desktop: the logo's left edge and the links' right edge against the content column
findings.fault: The mark starts at the margin line (about x 225) while the heading and every block start about 30 px further right. The last nav link ends past the photo's and the tiles' right edge. The bar's edges and the page's edges miss each other by a small, visible step.
findings.who_objects: A careful reader: near-miss alignment reads as sloppiness on a site selling precision in legal drafting.
